item.title: Organizational Outcomes Through Event Leverage: A New Research Agenda for Sport Organizations
item.content:encoded:
Marijke Taks, University of Ottawa

Paul Hover, Mulier Institute

Koen Breedveld, The Hague University of Applied Sciences

Event leverage research has traditionally focused on economic and social impacts, but organizational outcomes within sport organizations remain understudied. This special issue establishes organizational outcomes—sustainable changes resulting from strategic event leveraging—as a distinct research domain, encompassing effectiveness, governance, partnerships, volunteer systems, learning, innovation, and financial sustainability.

The special issue shifts focus to sport organizations as primary units of analysis within the sport ecosystem. Rather than treating organizational benefits as incidental byproducts, the call positions them as explicit strategic objectives. This responds to demands from governments and funding agencies for evidence that publicly funded events generate meaningful, sustained public value.

Contributions should advance conceptual and methodological foundations by integrating organizational capacity and institutional theory frameworks. The special issue seeks empirical, theoretical, and conceptual papers using innovative methods such as longitudinal designs and mixed methods to improve measurement of organizational outcomes across different contexts.

Appel publié par European Sport Management Quarterly. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Organizational outcomes in sport events
  • Event leverage theory
  • Organizational effectiveness and efficiency
  • Strategic partnerships in sport
  • Volunteer recruitment and retention
  • Organizational learning and innovation
  • Organizational capacity development
  • Financial sustainability of sport organizations
  • Governance in sport organizations
  • Sport ecosystem and stakeholder networks
  • Methodological approaches to measuring organizational change
  • Sport event legacy and impact evaluation
  • Policy implications of organizational outcomes

  • March 15, 2027: Full manuscript submission deadline

item.title: Personality in the Upper Echelons – Advancing Theory, Methods, and Context
item.content:encoded:
Upper echelons research has long argued that organizational outcomes reflect the characteristics of those who lead them. Scholars have shown that personality plays a central role in shaping how executives interpret information, make decisions, interact with stakeholders, and steer their organizations. Yet, despite a rapidly expanding literature on CEO personality and related constructs, recent reviews highlight persistent challenges: conceptual narrowness, methodological limitations, geographic concentration, and a tendency toward insularity rather than theoretical integration.

Appel publié par Journal of Managerial Psychology. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How do motives, values, traits, and narratives of organizational leaders shape firm behavior?
  • Under what conditions do personality effects strengthen or weaken?
  • How can scholars better measure personality in the upper echelons?
  • How do institutional, cultural, and governance contexts shape the expression and consequences of executive personality?
  • Broadening the conceptualization of executive personality beyond Big Five and narcissism traits
  • Integrating insights from personality psychology including motives, values, identity, and life stories
  • Mechanisms linking personality to strategic outcomes such as CSR, M&A, innovation, and risk-taking
  • Personality dynamics over time including personality change and developmental experiences
  • TMT dynamics, leadership styles, and power distributions shaped by executive personality
  • Contextual, cultural, and institutional moderators of personality effects across national cultures and governance systems
  • Measurement and assessment of executive personality using multi-method designs and unobtrusive indicators
  • Personality composition and complementarities within boards, TMTs, and collective leadership
  • CEO selection, evaluation, and succession planning incorporating personality
  • Executive personality influence on ethical decision making and societal outcomes
